macros.name: Comment
macros.doc: The \Comment command simply produces the comment symbol //, followed by a space.

macros.name: CommentSymbol
macros.doc: To get the comment symbol without a following space, use \CommentSymbol.

macros.name: const
macros.doc: We typeset constants such as NIL, TRUE, and RED in small caps with the \const command, e.g., \const{nil}, \const{true}, and \const{red}.

macros.name: Do
macros.doc: \Do increments the indentation level to start the body.

macros.name: ElseIf
macros.doc: For an if-ladder, use \Then for the first case, \ElseNoIf for the last case, and \ElseIf followed by \Then for all intermediate cases.

macros.name: func
macros.doc: We typeset the names of fixed functions in plain old roman with the \func command, e.g., level and out-degree.

macros.name: Goto
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: If
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: li
macros.doc: To start a new, numbered line, use the \li command.

macros.name: proc
macros.doc: For procedure names, use the \proc command. It typesets procedure names in small caps, and dashes (which occur frequently in our procedure names) are typeset as hyphens.

macros.name: Procname
macros.doc: The \Procname command specifies the name of the procedure.

macros.name: RComment
macros.doc: We used the command \RComment to justify a comment against the right margin.

macros.name: Return
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: Spawn
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: Startalign
macros.doc: The \Startalign command takes an argument that is the text string that you wish to align just to the right of.

macros.name: Stopalign
macros.doc: Use the \Stopalign command to restore indentation to its state from before the \Startalign command.

macros.name: Sync
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.doc: For an if-ladder, use \Then for the first case, \ElseNoIf for the last case, and \ElseIf followed by \Then for all intermediate cases.

macros.name: To
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: twodots
macros.doc: We denote subarrays with the “: :” notation, which is produced by the \twodots command.

macros.name: While
macros.doc: The following commands simply produce their corresponding keywords, typeset in boldface: \For, \To, \Downto, \By, \While, \If, \Return, \Goto (which does not appear in CLRS 3/e, but you might wish to use), \Error, \Spawn, \Sync, and \Parfor (which produces the compound keyword parallel for).

macros.name: zi
macros.doc: To start a new, unnumbered line, use the \zi command.

envs.name: codebox
envs.doc: A codebox is a section of code that does not break across pages.
